newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Skoda says H1 sales up 27.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Czech Skoda says H1 sales up 27.2 pct.

text.p: Skoda Automobilova a.s., majority owned by Volkwagen AG, said on Monday that its worldwide unit sales for the first half of the year had risen 27.2 percent, year-on-year, to 161,886 cars.
In a statement, Skoda said its domestic sales were up 17.5 percent to 51,945 cars, while sales to its largest export destination, Slovakia, were up 63.5 percent to 14,037.
The company has set a growth target of 30 percent or 340,000 cars to be produced and sold for the whole of 1997.
Among its different cars produced, Skoda said its top seller was still its Felicia hatchback which accounted for 95,061 of vehicles sold in the first half in 60 separate markets,

The Felicia Combi station wagon posted sales of 41,772 , the Felicia Pickup and Vanplus with 14,936 sold and the new Octavia mid-sized sedan with 12,252, 8,226 of which were sold in the Czech Republic.
